verdict.rationale: Elastic documents ad-hoc ES|QL queries, search and filter over all ingested logs in Discover, schema-agnostic ingestion, and a columnar engine 'engineered for high-cardinality'. Together these point to querying high-cardinality fields without pre-aggregation. However, the evidence never explicitly shows grouping by arbitrary fields such as user id or request id, nor confirms that no mapping or index definition is needed first. The high-cardinality claim is framed around time-series metrics. missing for 10: explicit group-by (e.g. STATS BY) on arbitrary high-cardinality fields, documentation that fields are queryable without prior mapping or index setup, independent or hands-on corroboration of high-cardinality query performance.

support.subject: As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first

citations.quote: Elastic is built on a columnar time series database engineered for high-cardinality
Elastic is open by design, schema-agnostic
Use **Discover** to search, filter, and tail all your logs ingested into your project in one place.
Ingest raw logs in any format directly to a single endpoint without the need for complex agent management or manual parsing pipelines.
